text: September fourteenth, nineteen sixty-eight. Five university workers from Puebla set out to climb the volcano, La Mah-leen-cheh. They only needed somewhere to sleep.
text0: September 14, 1968. Five university workers from Puebla set out to climb the volcano La Malinche. They only needed somewhere to sleep.

text: Heavy rain and nightfall forced them to stop in the village of San Mee-gel Kah-noh-ah. A local man, Loo-kas Gar-see-ah, offered them shelter in his home.
text0: Heavy rain and nightfall forced them to stop in the village of San Miguel Canoa. A local man, Lucas García, offered them shelter in his home.

text: But in Kah-noh-ah, the parish priest had been preaching fear. Communists, he warned, were coming.
text0: But in Canoa, the parish priest had been preaching fear. Communists, he warned, were coming.

text: That night, the church bells rang. Voices shouted that the communists had arrived… that they had come to kill, and to steal the women.
Nearly eight hundred people surrounded the house.
Two of the visitors, Heh-soos Kah-ree-yoh and Rah-mohn Goo-tee-eh-rez, were killed. So was Loo-kas, the man who took them in. Four people died. The three survivors were gravely injured.
text0: Two of the visitors, Jesús Carrillo and Ramón Gutiérrez, were killed. So was Lucas, the man who took them in. Four people died. The three survivors were gravely injured.

text: They were not agitators. They were hikers, looking for a place to sleep.
The priest accused of inciting the crowd was never convicted. There was no ghost in Kah-noh-ah. Only a rumor… and a crowd that believed it. This is Plot Twist, with A. and R.
